definition: Unpleasantness is the negative side of affect, referring to how bad or aversive an experience feels. In this context, it means participants’ felt discomfort during a fatiguing task, which can vary with psychological factors such as where attention is focused.

reasons: The packet supports unpleasantness as an affective measure during a fatiguing wall-sit task and shows it differed with attentional focus, but it does not support the broad general definition of unpleasantness as the “negative side of affect” or as a general property of any experience.
“Participants’ felt discomfort” is plausible from the study context, but the packet does not define unpleasantness as discomfort in general; it only reports reduced unpleasantness during the task.
The wording goes beyond the source by generalizing a specific experimental finding into a dictionary-style definition without direct support from the packet.
The packet does not explicitly support the claim that “unpleasantness is the negative side of affect,” nor that it refers to “how bad or aversive an experience feels.”

The packet only reports “pleasantness/unpleasantness” in the context of a wall-sit task and that external focus reduced “unpleasantness”; it does not define unpleasantness as “felt discomfort,” nor does it support that it “can vary with psychological factors such as where attention is focused” as a general definitional statement (it reports one study finding about attentional focus).
Some definitional wording (“negative side of affect,” “felt discomfort,” “can vary… such as”) goes beyond what is directly stated in the provided packet.
